task: On the prepared Ubuntu control node, inventory.yml and collect.yml are in the current directory. Check the playbook’s syntax without executing its IOS tasks.

teaching.hint: Choose validation, not a run or a host-list preview.
teaching.takeaway: A successful syntax check does not contact the router or validate its IOS command strings. A syntactically valid play can still fail at authentication, authorization or command execution.

task: collect.yml targets branch_routers, which contains r1 and r2 in inventory.yml. Before execution, display the eligible targets after limiting this run to r1. Both files are in the current directory.

teaching.hint: Preview the intersection of the play’s host selection and the run limit.
teaching.takeaway: The preview should contain only r1. A limit narrows the play’s eligible hosts; it cannot add a host excluded by that play, and listing hosts does not test SSH.

task: From the prepared Ubuntu project directory, execute the reviewed read-only collect.yml using inventory.yml, restricted to r1. Host identity and manual SSH are already verified; request the SSH password interactively.

teaching.hint: Select the playbook, inventory and limited target without storing the password in the command.
teaching.takeaway: This command performs the device tasks rather than merely listing or validating them. Compare returned device identity and command output with the baseline; an ok recap alone does not establish the required network state.

task: On the prepared Ubuntu control node, collect show clock once from r1 using the cisco.ios.ios_command module. Use inventory.yml, host group branch_routers, a limit of r1 and an interactive SSH-password prompt.
answer: ansible branch_routers -i inventory.yml -m cisco.ios.ios_command -a 'commands="show clock"' --limit r1 --ask-pass

teaching.hint: Use the one-off Ansible executable and keep the module argument together as one quoted value.
teaching.takeaway: The module sends show clock to IOS; the control-node shell does not execute it locally. A returned clock string proves command output was collected, not that the device has synchronized time.
